The Nasdaq fell 2.6% on AI-spending fears and the Philadelphia semiconductor index dropped 6.7%, while Brent crude pushed above $114 — its highest in over five months — on Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites and reports of renewed U.S./Israeli strikes on Iran. VIX sits near ~19 (+14% Thursday), and the 10Y plunged back below 5% in a flight to safety. Futures are mildly red into Friday’s open. The scanner boarded four names — T (A, bear), RCI (A, bull), WCN (C, bull), ALLE (C, bull) — but both Type A gaps printed on near-zero relative volume (far below the 1.3× bar) and the two Type C breakouts are same-day, unproven. An open-ended oil/geopolitical tail plus an AI wobble keeps P(≥1% gap) above the 35% trigger, so GREEN is locked out. Stand down on new credit spreads today, or push DTE past the conflict window.

focus.jnote: The environment stays defensive into Friday. AI-spending doubts and Middle East tensions are driving a global risk-off move, with chip stocks tumbling and Brent near $114 on Iran strike reports and attacks on Saudi oil sites. Brent crude climbed toward $114 per barrel on Friday, its highest level in over five months as escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi targets and reports of possible renewed U.S. strikes against Iran raised supply risks. Thursday was brutal for tech: the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.1% (2.6% on another read), the S&P 500 fell 1% and the Dow slipped 0.4%. The VIX rose 14.09% to 19.03. In a flight to safety, the 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.952%, down 19.3 basis points — its largest daily decline since March 2023. This remains a live, open-ended oil/geopolitical tail stacked on an AI-earnings wobble — not a premium-selling tape.
focus.notdown: RCI is the only boarded bull-put candidate, and it’s a thin one. Rogers reported Q3 results that surpassed estimates, posting adjusted EPS of CAD 1.29 (beating by CAD 0.05) on revenue of CAD 5.44 billion, driving a 4.57% after-hours gain. But the scanner flagged near-zero relative volume and no open-interest data — verify the chain manually. The two Type C breakouts (WCN, ALLE) are bullish by definition but same-day and unproven. On a RED, oil-shock morning the disciplined answer is watch-only, sell nothing new.
focus.notup: T is the only boarded bear-call — a Type A gap DOWN the tape actually backs. AT&T fell ~5.8% before the open despite beating — adjusted EPS of 65 cents on revenue of $32.3 billion topped estimates of 60 cents and $31.69 billion — as capex concerns overshadowed the top-line beat. Shares fell 6.4% on October 21. But the scanner flagged the reaction printed on near-zero relative volume. Selling bear calls into a VIX-rising, oil-shock tape invites a squeeze on any peace headline — stand aside or size tiny.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite ~68 is deep in WARM and P(≥1% gap) at ~45% is well above the 35% trigger — either alone locks out GREEN. More important than the numbers: an oil supply shock above $114 Brent on live Houthi/Iran-strike reports is an unscheduled, open-ended tail, the two Type A gaps (T, RCI) printed on near-zero relative volume below the 1.3× bar, and the two Type C breakouts (WCN, ALLE) are same-day, still proving themselves. Stand down on new credit spreads, or if you must be positioned, push DTE past the conflict window and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

setups.read: A Type A gap DOWN the tape backs — but a thin one, and a beat-and-fall. AT&T posted adjusted EPS of 65 cents on revenue of $32.3 billion, topping estimates of 60 cents and $31.69 billion. Yet the stock fell 6.4% on October 21 as postpaid phone net adds of 379,000 fell short of the ~387,410 expected and capex/SpaceX-competition concerns weighed, even as AT&T raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to ~$2.40. The scanner’s catch: the reaction printed on near-zero relative volume (0.02×, far below the 1.3× bar), the implied move was 3.7% vs a ~4.1% realized gap, and it noted the catalyst is two days old (Oct 21). Liquidity passed (OI ~2,390, ATM spread $0.09). On a RED day this is watch-only at most.
setups.check_note: On a RED day, don’t open new premium. If you must, half size at most and only at 9:35 if price < prior close (~$22.74) AND < today’s open AND in the lower third of range. Relative volume (0.02×) is the weak spot — want real turnover — and the catalyst is 2 sessions old, so the fresh gap may already be filling. No earnings inside DTE (next ~Jan 27, 2027).

setups.read: A Type A gap UP on a double beat — but confirm the figures before sizing. Rogers reported Q3 adjusted EPS of CAD 1.29, beating by CAD 0.05, on revenue of CAD 5.44 billion (up 1.7% YoY and CAD 43M above projections), driving a 4.57% after-hours gain. The company reaffirmed its 2026 outlook and highlighted record free cash flow. The scanner boarded it bullish off the price reaction but flagged that EPS/revenue weren’t wired from its usual source — verify the double-beat — and the gap printed on near-zero relative volume (0.00×) with no open-interest data returned. Implied move was 8.8% vs a ~2.1% realized gap. ATM spread $0.15 OK. On a RED day, watch-only.

setups.read: A fresh 52-week-high breakout on real volume — the day’s cleanest technical, but same-day and unproven. Waste Connections rose 9.9% to close at $184.88 on October 22, near its 52-week high of $186.93. The move followed an earnings beat — EPS of $1.58 vs $1.52 consensus, with revenue up 23.8% YoY to $2.64 billion — and a raised outlook plus a 10% dividend hike. The scanner confirmed breakout-day volume at 3.92× the 50-day average (well above the 1.3× bar) with price extended ~5.7% above the $174.33 pivot. But it’s a same-day breakout — still proving itself — and no open-interest data returned. ATM spread $0.90 OK. On a risk-off morning, breakouts fail easily; size accordingly.

risks: Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure — Iran-backed Houthi militants claimed attacks on Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea port of Yanbu plus strikes on an oil field and airport in the world’s largest crude exporter. Any further hit on Aramco facilities gaps the whole tape — the number-one thing to watch.

Oil & Strait of Hormuz — Brent traded at $114.00 and WTI at $100.40 as Middle East hostilities stayed front-page news. Any shipping incident sends crude (and jet fuel) vertical — the week’s biggest tail.

AI trade keeps cracking — the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 6.7% as Meta raised its 2026 AI spending outlook. Meta fell 7% on concerns about its capital commitments. A continued chip rollover drags the whole index lower.

Rates whipsaw after the flight to safety — the 10-year fell to 4.952% (down 19.3 bps), its largest daily drop in 3 years and 7 months, and its lowest since mid-September. A reversal on persistent oil-driven inflation fear could compound equity pressure; the Fed is in blackout before the Oct 27–28 FOMC.

Thin volume on the boarded A-gaps + same-day C-breakouts — T (0.02×) and RCI (0.00×) both printed well below the 1.3× bar, and WCN/ALLE are same-day breakouts into a risk-off open. Treat all four as half-size, confirm-at-9:35 watch-items at best on a RED day.

earnings.intro: Q3 season is at full stride — AT&T, Rogers, Waste Connections and Allegion all reported, and Tesla & Meta headlined Wednesday night.
